title: Deuteronomy Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 2:1, by which way did the Israelites take their journey into the wilderness?
options: By the way of the Red sea
By the way of the Jordan river
Through the land of the Moabites
Along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea
questions.correctAnswer: By the way of the Red sea
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:1 states that the journey was taken into the wilderness by the way of the Red sea, as the LORD commanded.

questions.question: What command did the LORD give regarding Mount Seir in Deuteronomy 2:3?
options: Build an altar on the mountain
questions.correctAnswer: Turn you northward
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:3 says, 'Ye have compassed this mountain long enough: turn you northward.'

questions.question: Who are described as the brethren through whose coast the Israelites were to pass, according to Deuteronomy 2:4?
questions.correctAnswer: The children of Esau
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:4 instructs to pass through the coast of your brethren the children of Esau, who dwell in Seir.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 2:5 commands the Israelites to take land from the children of Esau.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:5 states 'Meddle not with them; for I will not give you of their land, no, not so much as a foot breadth.'

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 2:6, how were the Israelites to obtain meat and water from the children of Esau?
questions.correctAnswer: By buying them for money
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:6 commands to buy meat and water from them for money to eat and drink.

questions.question: How long had the LORD been with the Israelites in the wilderness according to Deuteronomy 2:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Forty years
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:7 says the LORD has been with them these forty years in the wilderness, providing for all their needs.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 2:8 says the Israelites passed through the wilderness of Moab after passing the children of Esau.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:8 states that after passing Esau's children, they passed by the way of the wilderness of Moab.

questions.question: What did the LORD command about the Moabites in Deuteronomy 2:9?
options: Do not distress or battle them
questions.correctAnswer: Do not distress or battle them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:9 commands not to distress or contend with the Moabites because their land is given to the children of Lot.

questions.question: Who does Deuteronomy 2:10 say were great, many, and tall like the Anakims?
questions.correctAnswer: The Emims
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:10 describes the Emims as a great, many, and tall people like the Anakims.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 2:12, who succeeded the Horims in Seir?
questions.correctAnswer: The children of Esau
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:12 says the children of Esau succeeded the Horims after destroying them and dwelt in their stead.

questions.question: What action did the narrator command in Deuteronomy 2:13?
options: Rise up and cross the brook Zered
Build an altar on the mountain
questions.correctAnswer: Rise up and cross the brook Zered
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:13 records the command to rise up and get over the brook Zered.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 2:14, the Israelites wandered in the wilderness for thirty-eight years before crossing the brook Zered.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:14 states the space from Kadeshbarnea until crossing the brook Zered was thirty-eight years.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD gave the children of Esau the land of Seir as their possession, according to Deuteronomy 2:5.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:5 affirms that the LORD gave mount Seir to Esau for a possession.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 2, which command comes before all the others listed here?
options: Turn northward after compassing Mount Seir
Buy meat and water from the children of Esau
Rise up and cross the brook Zered
questions.correctAnswer: Turn northward after compassing Mount Seir
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:3 commands turning northward after compassing Mount Seir, which comes before the other commands in later verses.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 2:7, what has the LORD blessed the Israelites in?
options: All the works of their hand
questions.correctAnswer: All the works of their hand
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:7 states the LORD hath blessed the Israelites in all the works of their hand.

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How long did the Israelites wander from Kadeshbarnea until they crossed the brook Zered?
questions.correctAnswer: 38 years
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:14 states that the space from Kadeshbarnea until crossing the brook Zered was thirty and eight years, marking the time until the generation of men of war was wasted as the LORD had sworn.

questions.question: What was the reason given for the destruction of the men of war among the Israelites?
options: The hand of the LORD was against them
questions.correctAnswer: The hand of the LORD was against them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:15 explains that indeed the hand of the LORD was against the men of war to destroy them from among the host until they were consumed, fulfilling His judgment.

questions.question: What command did the LORD give regarding the Moabites as the Israelites passed through their land?
options: Distress not the Moabites, neither contend with them in battle
Engage in battle and take possession
Ignore their presence and pass through quickly
questions.correctAnswer: Distress not the Moabites, neither contend with them in battle
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:9 commands not to distress the Moabites or contend with them because their land was given to the children of Lot, showing the LORD's sovereign distribution of land.

questions.question: Who were the Emims, as described in Deuteronomy 2?
options: A people great, many, and tall, accounted giants like the Anakims
Priests in the land of Moab
questions.correctAnswer: A people great, many, and tall, accounted giants like the Anakims
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:10-11 describes the Emims as a great and tall people, called giants like the Anakims, highlighting the formidable inhabitants of the land before Israel's arrival.

questions.question: What instruction did the LORD give about the children of Ammon as the Israelites approached their land?
options: Do not distress or meddle with them
Buy provisions from them without fear
Make a treaty with them for land
questions.correctAnswer: Do not distress or meddle with them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:19 instructs the Israelites not to distress or meddle with the children of Ammon because their land was given to the children of Lot, emphasizing respect for God's allotment.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 2 teach us about God's faithfulness and provision over the wilderness journey?
options: God was with the Israelites for 40 years and they lacked nothing
They were left to rely solely on their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: God was with the Israelites for 40 years and they lacked nothing
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:7 notes that the LORD blessed the Israelites in all their works and was with them through the wilderness for forty years, ensuring they lacked nothing, demonstrating His faithful provision.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 2:24 promise will happen when the Israelites contend with Sihon the Amorite?
options: The LORD has given Sihon and his land into Israel's hand to possess
They will face defeat and must retreat
They will only gain partial victory
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD has given Sihon and his land into Israel's hand to possess
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:24 affirms that the LORD gave Sihon, king of Heshbon, and his land into Israel's hand, instructing them to possess it and contend in battle, highlighting divine promise in obedience.

questions.question: What was the purpose of sending messengers with words of peace to Sihon king of Heshbon?
options: To request passage through his land without conflict
To declare war and demand surrender
To challenge him to a duel
questions.correctAnswer: To request passage through his land without conflict
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:26-27 shows that messengers were sent to Sihon with words of peace, asking to pass through his land by the highway without turning aside, indicating an initial pursuit of peaceful passage.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 2, the LORD hardened Sihon's heart to deliver him into Israel's hand.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:30 explains that the LORD hardened Sihon's spirit and made his heart obstinate so that he would be delivered into Israel's hand, showing God's sovereign control over the outcome.

questions.question: What did the Israelites do after defeating Sihon and taking his cities?
options: Utterly destroyed all men, women, and children, leaving none alive
Allowed the inhabitants to remain as servants
Made peace treaties with the survivors
questions.correctAnswer: Utterly destroyed all men, women, and children, leaving none alive
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:34 states that after taking Sihon's cities, the Israelites utterly destroyed all men, women, and little ones, leaving none to remain, demonstrating complete conquest as commanded.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 2:25, what effect would Israel's victory have on the nations under the whole heaven?
options: They would fear and tremble at the report of Israel
They would seek to ally with Israel immediately
They would increase their own armies
questions.correctAnswer: They would fear and tremble at the report of Israel
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:25 states that the LORD would put dread and fear of Israel upon all nations under heaven, causing them to tremble and be in anguish when they hear reports of Israel's victories.

questions.question: What practical lesson about obedience and trust in God can be drawn from the Israelites' approach to Sihon and the land of Moab and Ammon?
options: Obey God’s commands precisely, trusting His instructions about which battles to fight and which to avoid
Ignore divine instructions and conquer all lands for safety
Seek peace with every nation regardless of God’s direction
Avoid conflict at all costs, even against enemies God has given into your hand
questions.correctAnswer: Obey God’s commands precisely, trusting His instructions about which battles to fight and which to avoid
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:9,19,24 illustrate that Israel was commanded not to contend with Moabites or Ammonites but to fight Sihon as God directed, teaching that trusting and obeying God’s specific instructions leads to success and faithfulness.

questions.question: True or False: The descendants of Esau succeeded the Horims in Seir after destroying them, similar to how Israel succeeded in the land given by the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:12 states that the Horims dwelt in Seir beforetime, but the children of Esau succeeded them after destroying them, paralleling Israel's inheritance of the land given by the LORD.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 2:28–29 teach about the Israelites’ interaction with the children of Esau and the Moabites during their journey?
options: They bought meat and water for money and passed through on foot
questions.correctAnswer: They bought meat and water for money and passed through on foot
questions.explanation: Verses 28 and 29 explain that the Israelites requested to buy meat and water for money and only pass through on foot, following the example of their peaceful dealings with Esau’s descendants and Moabites, showing integrity and respect.

questions.question: True or False: The Israelites were forbidden by the LORD to enter the land of the children of Ammon or the region by the river Jabbok.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:37 indicates that the Israelites came not into the land of the children of Ammon, nor to places by the river Jabbok or cities in the mountains, as the LORD had forbidden them, showing obedience to divine boundaries.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 2.

questions.question: What was the reason given for Sihon king of Heshbon's refusal to let Israel pass through his land?
options: He was afraid of Israel's strength
The LORD hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate
He had a treaty with the children of Ammon
He wanted to sell them meat and water
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:30 states that Sihon's refusal was because the LORD hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, so he might be delivered into Israel's hand.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 2, what instruction was given about buying food and water from the children of Esau?
options: Buy meat and water for money from them
Take food and water without payment
questions.correctAnswer: Buy meat and water for money from them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:6 commands to buy meat and water for money from the children of Esau rather than taking it freely.

questions.question: Which peoples are described in Deuteronomy 2 as giants similar to the Anakims?
questions.correctAnswer: Emims, Zamzummims, and Anakims
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:10-11 and 2:20-21 describe the Emims and Zamzummims as giant peoples similar to the Anakims.

questions.question: What was the result of Israel's battle with Sihon and his people?
options: They made peace and paid tribute
The LORD delivered Sihon into Israel's hands and they defeated him
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD delivered Sihon into Israel's hands and they defeated him
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:33 confirms that the LORD delivered Sihon before Israel, and they smote him and his people.

questions.question: Which land was Israel forbidden to possess according to Deuteronomy 2:37?
options: The land of the children of Ammon
questions.correctAnswer: The land of the children of Ammon
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:37 states Israel did not come to possess the land of the children of Ammon or areas forbidden by the LORD.

questions.question: What was the attitude Israel was commanded to have when passing through the land of the children of Esau and Moab?
options: To wage war and take land by force
To avoid distressing or contending with them
To conquer and destroy their cities
questions.correctAnswer: To avoid distressing or contending with them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:4-5 and 2:9 instruct not to meddle with or distress the children of Esau and Moab as God gave their lands to them.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Deuteronomy 2 to describe the succession of peoples dwelling in lands before Israel?
options: Typology showing Israel as a new Adam
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm illustrating conquest and succession
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:12, 2:21-22 show a chiasm pattern describing how one people succeeded another by conquest, illustrating a literary structure of rise and fall.

questions.question: What Hebrew meaning of the word 'Zered' (the brook mentioned in verse 13) can be inferred based on its context in Deuteronomy 2?
questions.correctAnswer: A flowing or moving water
questions.explanation: The brook Zered (Deuteronomy 2:13) refers to a water body, and the Hebrew root suggests flowing or moving water, fitting its context as a crossing point.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of the LORD hardening a king’s heart to accomplish His purposes, similar to Sihon’s story in Deuteronomy 2?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 9:12 - Pharaoh's heart hardened
questions.explanation: Like Sihon in Deuteronomy 2:30, Pharaoh’s heart was hardened by God in Exodus 9:12 to fulfill divine purposes.

questions.question: What was the purpose of Israel's request to pass through Sihon's land according to Deuteronomy 2:27-28?
options: To conquer and settle the land
To pass through quietly buying food and water
questions.correctAnswer: To pass through quietly buying food and water
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:27-28 explains Israel’s peaceful request to pass through, buying meat and water, without turning aside.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 2:25 foreshadow Israel’s reputation among the nations after defeating Sihon?
options: Nations will tremble and be in anguish at Israel's report
Israel will be forgotten among the nations
Nations will form alliances with Israel
Israel will become a land of exile
questions.correctAnswer: Nations will tremble and be in anguish at Israel's report
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:25 predicts that Israel’s victory will cause dread and fear among the nations under heaven.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 2:5, Israel was allowed to take even a footbreadth of Esau’s land.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:5 explicitly forbids Israel from taking any part of Esau’s land, not even a footbreadth.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 2:7 says that during the forty years in the wilderness, Israel lacked nothing because the LORD blessed their works and knew their journey.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:7 states that the LORD blessed Israel in all their works and they lacked nothing during their wilderness journey.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament book contains a parallel account of Israel’s conquest over Sihon as described in Deuteronomy 2?
questions.correctAnswer: Numbers 21
questions.explanation: Numbers 21 recounts the defeat of Sihon king of the Amorites, parallel to the account in Deuteronomy 2.

questions.question: Which theme in Deuteronomy 2 is fulfilled in the New Testament by Jesus' teaching on peace and non-violence?
options: Passing peacefully through lands buying food and water
questions.correctAnswer: Passing peacefully through lands buying food and water
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:27-29's theme of peaceful passage foreshadows Jesus' teachings on non-violence and peace (Matthew 5:9).

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by God's instruction not to seize any land of the children of Esau but to buy food and water from them?
options: The doctrine of God’s sovereign distribution of land
The doctrine of salvation by faith alone
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God’s sovereign distribution of land
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:4-6 explains that God has given Mount Seir to Esau for a possession, and Israel must not take it by force but buy from them. This reveals God's sovereign authority over the distribution of nations and territories.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated by His guidance and provision during Israel's 40 years in the wilderness?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:7 shows God’s providence as He blesses Israel in all their works and provides for their needs throughout 40 years in the wilderness, ensuring they lack nothing.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 2:9-12 connect to the broader redemptive story of God's justice and judgment?
options: By showing God's judgment on giant nations before Israel's inheritance
By predicting the coming Messiah's birth
By illustrating the Mosaic Law's holiness
questions.correctAnswer: By showing God's judgment on giant nations before Israel's inheritance
questions.explanation: Verses 9-12 describe God’s judgment on the Emims and Horims, giants who previously occupied the land. This judgment paves the way for Israel’s inheritance, showing God's justice before fulfilling His redemptive promises.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by the fact that God forbade Israel from contending with Moab and Ammon, giving their lands to the descendants of Lot instead?
options: God’s faithfulness to His covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness to His covenant promises
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:9 and 2:19 reveal that God honors previous land grants to the descendants of Lot, demonstrating His faithfulness to all His promises, not just those to Israel.

questions.question: What attribute of God is illustrated by His hardening of Sihon’s heart to bring about Israel’s victory?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:30 reveals God’s sovereign control over human hearts, as He hardened Sihon’s spirit to fulfill His divine plan of delivering his land to Israel.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 2:24-25, what is the significance of God putting 'the dread' and 'fear' of Israel upon the nations under heaven?
options: It demonstrates God's power to glorify His people
It shows Israel's military superiority by human strength
It indicates God’s abandonment of other nations
It predicts the coming exile of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God's power to glorify His people
questions.explanation: Verses 24-25 show God actively instilling fear of Israel among the nations, highlighting His power to exalt His people as part of His redemptive plan.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Deuteronomy 2:5-6 and 2:28-29 reveal about Israel’s conduct among other nations?
options: Respect for others’ possessions and reliance on God’s provision
questions.correctAnswer: Respect for others’ possessions and reliance on God’s provision
questions.explanation: Both passages instruct Israel not to seize land unjustly but to buy food and water as they travel, showing respect for others’ property and dependence on God’s guidance (Deuteronomy 2:5-6, 28-29).

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 2:14-15 contribute to the understanding of God’s judgment on the generation of men of war?
options: It shows God’s righteous judgment leading to the removal of unbelief
It indicates God’s rejection of Israel entirely
It highlights Israel’s failure to obey the law
It explains the origin of the Mosaic covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s righteous judgment leading to the removal of unbelief
questions.explanation: Verses 14-15 explain that the men of war were destroyed as God’s judgment because of their disobedience, allowing a new generation to inherit the promises.

questions.question: What narrative arc does the crossing of the brook Zered and the 38 years of wandering highlight in the broader redemptive history of Israel?
options: The establishment of the Davidic kingdom
The giving of the Ten Commandments
questions.correctAnswer: Transition from judgment to inheritance
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:13-14 marks the end of the wilderness wanderings and the passing of the disobedient generation, signifying transition toward possessing the promised land.

questions.question: What theological truth is taught by the complete destruction of Sihon’s cities and people, sparing only the livestock and spoil, as recorded in Deuteronomy 2:33-35?
options: God’s judgment includes both mercy and justice
God is indifferent to human suffering
God’s covenant is conditional on animal sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment includes both mercy and justice
questions.explanation: Verses 33-35 show God’s justice in destroying wicked nations while sparing spoil and cattle for Israel, reflecting a balance of judgment and provision.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s hardening of hearts violates human free will. What does Deuteronomy 2:30 teach about this divine action?
options: God sovereignly uses human decisions within His plan without negating responsibility
God forces people to sin against their will
God’s hardening is arbitrary and unjust
God does not intervene in human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly uses human decisions within His plan without negating responsibility
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:30 shows God hardening Sihon’s heart to fulfill His purposes, demonstrating divine sovereignty that works through human choices while upholding moral accountability (cf. Romans 9:17-18).

questions.question: What does the mention of giant peoples like the Emims and Zamzummims in Deuteronomy 2 reveal about the spiritual and physical challenges Israel faced?
options: Israel's conquest required God's power over formidable foes
Israel conquered by their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: Israel's conquest required God's power over formidable foes
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 and 20-21 describe giants as previous inhabitants, emphasizing the need for God’s powerful intervention in Israel’s conquest.

questions.question: What combined theological lesson do Deuteronomy 2:22 and 2:23 teach about God’s judgment and the succession of peoples?
options: God’s justice results in the removal of wicked peoples and succession by others
God’s covenant is only with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice results in the removal of wicked peoples and succession by others
questions.explanation: Verses 22-23 reveal that God brought judgment on the Horims and Avims, allowing other peoples to succeed them, demonstrating God’s sovereign justice and historical fulfillment.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 2:17-19 reveal God’s consistent faithfulness in His promises to Israel regarding land possession?
options: God commands Israel to pass through Ar and not to distress Ammon, showing His commitment to previous promises
God allows Israel to take all lands by force
God’s promises are conditional on Israel’s military success
questions.correctAnswer: God commands Israel to pass through Ar and not to distress Ammon, showing His commitment to previous promises
questions.explanation: Verses 17-19 show God directing Israel to respect lands already given to others, demonstrating His unwavering faithfulness to all His covenant promises.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 2:36-37 teach about the limits of Israel’s conquest according to God’s command?
options: Israel was divinely restricted from entering Ammonite lands and other forbidden places
Israel conquered all surrounding nations without limit
Israel was allowed to settle anywhere
questions.correctAnswer: Israel was divinely restricted from entering Ammonite lands and other forbidden places
questions.explanation: Verses 36-37 state that Israel conquered many cities but was forbidden by God from entering the land of Ammon and certain other areas, showing divine boundaries are part of His plan.
